check: live chess.com verification of the M3 adapter (one-off, not part of the pass/fail suite)

method.extension: the SHIPPED extension/ directory (no manifest variant, no test-only matches)
method.page: https://www.chess.com/game/live/186394589423 (public finished blitz game; URL taken from the public chess.com API)
method.collector: the side panel document opened as a tab, raw chrome.runtime GameState listener
method.ground_truth: the game's official PGN from https://api.chess.com/pub/player/hikaru/games/2026/10 replayed with python-chess (independent rules engine)

state_sequence.reason: board found but neither its position nor a move list could be read
state_sequence.note: chess.com's pre-JS skeleton board (a CSS-sprite .board without .piece children) — the adapter reports it honestly, then re-emits when the real board appears

warnings: side to move inferred from active-clock; castling/en-passant/move counters unknown
state_sequence.note: pieces rendered before the move list: degraded metadata is flagged, not guessed silently

final_state.movesUci: 142 plies, byte-equal to the PGN replay

also_verified_live_same_day.skeleton_board: chess.com keeps a visible, same-sized #board.board skeleton div alongside/after load — the adapter prefers wc-chess-board over it (regression-trapped in test/fixtures/generate_chesscom.py)
also_verified_live_same_day.flipped_board: the play-computer side selector for black adds class="flipped" to wc-chess-board; piece square classes stay absolute
also_verified_live_same_day.internal_api: wc-chess-board.game.getFEN()/getHistorySANs() returned the same position/history (used only as fallback/cross-check)

what_this_does_not_cover: the real side-panel container (the collector ran in the panel document opened as a tab)
interaction (clicking the panel buttons by hand) — covered by the manual checklist in docs/HANDOFF.md
